subject: CarePath hosting posture — sizing, compliance checklist & MAP
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Emily Stone <emily.stone@carepathhealth.com>, procurement@carepathhealth.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-09-05T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: CarePath hosting posture — sizing, compliance checklist & MAP

Hi Emily / CarePath team,

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Per our call, I've attached the security questionnaire you requested and an initial sizing workbook that sketches two hosting paths: (A) Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool w/ tenant isolation) and (B) Redwood Private (customer-managed VPC / on-prem package).

Quick high-level contrasts we modeled in the spreadsheet:
- Isolation level: Dedicated = logical isolation + encrypted tenant volumes; Private = network isolation + customer KMS/HSM options.
- Capacity unit assumptions: we used a baseline of 2,000 monthly active LLM sessions (avg 350 tokens/session, 1.2k tokens peak), and 500 concurrent sessions at peak.
- Resource mapping (rough): Dedicated path = 4 x A100-80GB per 500 concurrent sessions (mixed batching); Private path = recommended 6 x A100-80GB (headroom for on-prem throughput variability + maintenance windows).

Notes / asks:
1) Please confirm whether you need complete air-gapped on-prem (no egress allowed) or a VPC-hosted Private deployment with outbound lines for software updates — this changes the baseline sizing and ops assumptions.
2) Attach any expected monthly token volume or concurrency targets (the attached workbook has editable cells).

Next step: I propose we sketch a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that aligns procurement milestones, security evidence delivery, and a short pilot (2–4 weeks) on a reduced footprint. I started a MAP draft and attached it for review.

If it helps, Karthik and Naomi are looping in infrastructure sizing options and timelines.

Thanks — talk soon,

--
Marissa Cole

From: Emily Stone <emily.stone@carepathhealth.com>

Subject: Re: CarePath hosting posture — sizing, compliance checklist & MAP

Marissa,

Thanks for the quick follow-up and the workbook. A few clarifications from our security team:
- We require a Private deployment option that supports customer-managed KMS (HSM preferred) and will likely need an air-gapped mode for certain PHI flows during the pilot.
- Procurement: our standard SLAs require a 99.9% uptime target for production, but pilot can be SLA-exempt.
- Expected load (pilot): ~1200 MA sessions/mo with peaks at 200 concurrent sessions and average payloads ~900 tokens. Production expectations to be determined after pilot.

I'll circulate the completed questionnaire by EOD Tuesday. Can you confirm whether the Private on-prem footprint in your workbook assumes on-site GPUs owned by CarePath or a colocated cluster managed by Redwood within CarePath's VPC? That distinction impacts procurement and cost models on our side.

Also, please send a short note on audit evidence timelines for SOC2 + penetration test reports.

Best,
Emily

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.inference>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-09-07T08:25:00-07:00
Subject: RE: sizing assumptions for CarePath (internal)

Team — internal sizing notes and counter-proposals based on Emily's reply:

Summary of updated pilot inputs from CarePath: 1200 MA / mo, peaks ~200 concurrent, avg payload 900 tokens. They require Private with customer KMS and potential air-gap for PHI flows.

Sizing math (quick):
- Baseline workload: 200 concurrent sessions * 900 tokens/session = 180k tokens in flight. Using model mix MPT-20 / Llama-3 style throughput on A100s (quantized), we estimate sustained token throughput per A100-80GB of ~80k tokens/sec when aggressively batched (pilot expected to be latency-sensitive; we should lower batch expectations). Conservatively: 40k tokens/sec usable per A100 for latency SLOs (~95th pct).
- For 200 concurrent, with average reply length ~900 tokens and expected interleaving, we get estimated steady demand ~18k tokens/sec (approx). That suggests 1 A100 could cover pilot peak on pure throughput but leaves no headroom, so we recommend 2 x A100-80GB to provide redundancy + patch windows.

Private vs Dedicated impact on hardware counts:
- Private (customer-owned or colocated with HSM): recommend 2 x A100 for pilot, plan to scale to 4–6 x A100 for production depending on growth. Additional ops burden: customer infra team must accept maintenance windows and host-level monitoring hooks.
- Dedicated (Redwood managed reserved fleet): recommend 2 x A100 for pilot as well but we can burst across multi-tenant reserved capacity for traffic spikes. Security posture differs: Dedicated provides tenant isolation and encrypted volumes, but not full air-gap.

Operational asks for MAP:
- Security evidence delivery timeline (SOC2 report, pentest memo): Naomi to confirm availability windows.
- Pilot runbook: onboarding checklist, egress configuration for updates, rollback plan. Jonas — can you draft an ops runbook template for a Private pilot (colocated) by 09/09?

I'll drop the updated numbers into the spreadsheet and flag the cells for Marissa to send to CarePath.

Karthik

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>

Date: 2026-09-08T14:35:00-07:00
Subject: RE: CarePath hosting posture — sizing, compliance checklist & MAP

Emily — thanks for the details and for confirming pilot expectations. Attaching a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP_CarePath_20260908.pdf) that reflects what we discussed: pilot timeline, who provides what evidence and when, procurement milestones, and a suggested pilot footprint (2 x A100-80GB colocated, HSM integration window = week 2).

Key bullets from the MAP:
- Pilot footprint: 2 x A100-80GB colocated with customer KMS/HSM access (Redwood-managed stack; customer-controlled keys).
- Security evidence: Redwood to provide last SOC2 Type II report and latest pentest memo by 2026-09-10. Naomi — can you confirm and attach to HubSpot?
- Pilot duration: 3 weeks (sanity + load), with an option to convert to Dedicated reserved capacity after validation.
- Acceptance criteria: functional parity with API, <200ms tail latency for 95th percentile on single-turn prompts, and no data exfil on air-gapped PHI flows during test.

Action items:
1) Emily: return signed MAP draft + completed questionnaire (target 2026-09-10).
2) Naomi: upload SOC2 + pentest memo to HS-4821 by 2026-09-10.
3) Jonas: pilot ops runbook (colocated) by 2026-09-09.
4) Karthik: finalize sizing tab and put recommended production scaling ladder into spreadsheet.

I'll follow up with a short call invite to walk the MAP and confirm on-site/colocation logistics.

Cheers,
Marissa
